description: Blockchain Village focuses on cryptocurrency security, smart contract auditing, DeFi flash loan exploits, hardware wallet reverse engineering, MEV sandwich attacks, and consensus defense.

talks.title: Flash Loans Demystified: DeFi Arbitrage & Oracle Attacks
talks.teaser: Anto Joseph demystifies flash loans in Decentralized Finance (DeFi), analyzing how uncollateralized loans enable multi-million dollar price oracle manipulation attacks.
talks.summary:
The Mechanics of Uncollateralized Flash Loans

Flash loans allow users to borrow millions of dollars in cryptocurrency assets with zero collateral, provided the borrowed capital is returned within the exact same atomic transaction block.

Legitimate DeFi Use Cases vs. Weaponization

Anto Joseph contrasts legitimate flash loan applications (such as DEX arbitrage and automated liquidations) with offensive exploits targeting vulnerable liquidity pools.

Deconstructing Price Oracle Manipulation Attacks

Joseph demonstrates how attackers use massive flash-borrowed capital to temporarily distort Automated Market Maker (AMM) spot prices, draining lending protocols.

Strategies for Smart Contract Defense

The presentation outlines mitigation architectures, including integrating decentralized time-weighted average price (TWAP) oracles and Chainlink data feeds.

talks.title: Will Secure Elements Strengthen Crypto Wallets? Hardware Security Auditing
talks.teaser: Byeongcheol Yoo evaluates hardware cryptocurrency wallets, analyzing whether Secure Elements (SE) effectively defend private keys against physical attacks.
talks.summary:
Software vs. Hardware Cryptocurrency Wallets

While software wallets store private keys on internet-connected hosts vulnerable to malware, hardware wallets isolate cryptographic seed phrases within dedicated microcontroller silicon.

Architecture and Role of Secure Elements (SE)

Byeongcheol Yoo explains the security mechanisms of Common Criteria certified Secure Elements, designed to resist physical tampering and side-channel leakage.

Auditing Hardware Wallet Physical Attack Surfaces

Yoo examines vulnerability classes affecting hardware wallets—including supply chain interdiction, fault injection (voltage glitching), and bus sniffing.

Designing Resilient Hardware Cryptographic Storage

The author provides hardware manufacturers with secure chip selection guidelines and firmware attestation protocols.

talks.title: Scaling Blockchains: A Novel Approach
talks.teaser: Colin Cantrell presents an alternative cryptographic and architectural approach to solving the blockchain trilemma of scalability, decentralization, and security.

talks.title: Understanding Unlimited Approval in Ethereum: ERC-20 Allowance Risks
talks.teaser: Dabao Wong reveals the systemic security risks of 'unlimited token approvals' in ERC-20 smart contracts, showing how vulnerable DApps lead to total wallet drains.
talks.summary:
The Ubiquity of the ERC-20 Token Standard

Decentralized applications (DApps) and DEXs rely on the ERC-20 approve() function to allow smart contracts to transfer tokens on a user's behalf.

The Anti-Pattern of Unlimited Approvals

Dabao Wong explains why DApps routinely request users to grant infinite token allowances ($2^{256}-1$) to avoid repetitive gas fees for each transaction.

Exploiting Lingering Allowances in Compromised DApps

Wong demonstrates how an attacker who discovers a vulnerability in a legacy DApp contract can drain tokens directly from users who approved the contract years earlier.

Safer Token Approval Paradigms

The author reviews mitigation frameworks, including ERC-2612 permit signatures, allowance revocation tools, and browser wallet permission warnings.

talks.title: Preventing Sandwich Attacks: MEV & Front-Running Defense in DeFi
talks.teaser: Gokul Alex and Tejaswa Rastogi dissect Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) sandwich attacks on decentralized exchanges, presenting defensive anti-frontrunning protocols.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Maximal Extractable Value (MEV)

Public blockchain mempools allow predatory bots to monitor pending decentralized exchange transactions and front-run high-value trades for guaranteed profit.

Deconstructing Sandwich Attacks on AMMs

Gokul Alex and Tejaswa Rastogi explain how sandwich bots execute a front-run buy order to inflate asset prices, allow the victim's trade to clear at maximum slippage, and back-run sell.

Measuring the Economic Impact on DeFi Traders

The speakers quantify the millions of dollars extracted from retail traders daily across Uniswap and SushiSwap liquidity pools.

Architecting Private Mempools and Slippage Guards

The authors review mitigation solutions—including Flashbots Protect private RPC endpoints, dynamic slippage tolerance algorithms, and MEV-resistant AMM designs.

talks.title: Subtle Ways to Lose Your Cryptocurrency: Malware, Clipboard Hijackers, & OpSec
talks.teaser: Josh McIntyre reviews subtle attack vectors that result in permanent cryptocurrency loss, covering clipboard hijackers, phishing dApps, and user operational errors.
talks.summary:
The Irreversibility of Cryptocurrency Loss

Unlike traditional financial institutions with fraud protection and chargebacks, blockchain transactions are immutable, making lost or stolen funds permanently unrecoverable.

Analyzing Modern Crypto Malware and Scams

Josh McIntyre breaks down prevalent cryptocurrency attack vectors—including clipboard address replacers, malicious browser extensions, and seed phrase credential harvesting.

Operational Pitfalls and Human Error

McIntyre examines how subtle operational mistakes—such as entering incorrect network chain IDs or misplacing non-deterministic backups—result in catastrophic fund loss.

A Pragmatic Security Framework for Crypto Users

The author provides a comprehensive operational security checklist covering hardware isolation, multisig governance, and transaction verification.

talks.title: Ethereum Hacks & How to Stop Them: OpenZeppelin Defender
talks.teaser: OpenZeppelin security architect Michael Lewellen reviews major smart contract hacks and demonstrates automated incident response using Defender.

talks.title: COSTA: Coinbase Secure Trait Analyzer & 2021 Crypto Threat Trends
talks.teaser: Coinbase principal researcher Peter Kacherginsky presents COSTA, an automated threat analyzer tracking exchange hacks, cross-chain DeFi bugs, and NFT scams.
talks.summary:
The Expanding Threat Landscape of Blockchain in 2021

The cryptocurrency ecosystem has experienced an unprecedented surge in sophisticated attacks—spanning cross-chain bridge exploits, flash loan drains, and NFT smart contract hacks.

Introducing COSTA: Coinbase Secure Trait Analyzer

Peter Kacherginsky presents COSTA, an automated threat intelligence and static analysis framework developed by Coinbase to categorize risky smart contract traits.

Threat Modeling Cross-Chain Bridges and DeFi Protocols

Kacherginsky analyzes major 2021 security incidents, mapping recurring vulnerability classes across decentralized finance (DeFi) and layer-1 consensus layers.

Building Automated Blockchain Threat Hunting Pipelines

The author shares methodologies for integrating automated telemetry scanners into exchange listing pipelines and continuous on-chain monitoring.

talks.title: Blockchain Village CTF Contest
talks.teaser: Reddcoin and TechAdept introduce the DEF CON 29 Blockchain Village CTF, featuring cryptographic challenges, consensus exploits, and smart contract puzzles.

talks.title: Blockchain as a Threat Modeling Tool: Collaborative Risk Assessment
talks.teaser: Korea University researchers Shinchul Park and Seungjoo Kim explore using blockchain consensus as a collaborative framework for multi-stakeholder threat modeling.
talks.summary:
The Challenge of Multi-Stakeholder Threat Modeling

Threat modeling complex enterprise systems requires input from diverse stakeholders whose differing priorities often introduce subjective bias and uneven evaluation weights.

Leveraging Blockchain for Decentralized Consensus

Shinchul Park and Seungjoo Kim propose utilizing blockchain architecture to record, validate, and reach democratic consensus on system threat models.

Designing the Decentralized Threat Modeling Protocol

The authors detail a framework where security analysts contribute threat vectors, assess likelihood and impact scores, and immutably record verified mitigations.

Evaluating Objectivity and Verifiability in Risk Assessment

The presentation demonstrates how decentralized threat registries eliminate single points of failure and enhance transparency in critical infrastructure defense.

talks.title: Surviving 51% Attacks: Proof-of-Work Consensus Resiliency
talks.teaser: Yaz Khoury examines 51% hashpower attacks on Proof-of-Work blockchains, analyzing chain reorganization defenses and checkpointing mechanisms.
